sources.entry: python-dotenv - Reads key-value pairs from a .env file and sets them as environment variables.

summary.one_liner: python-dotenv is a Python library and CLI that reads key-value pairs from a .env file and sets them as environment variables, aimed at 12-factor app development.
summary.what_it_does: Provides load_dotenv(), which reads a .env file (searching the script's directory and parents) and adds its variables to os.environ without overriding existing ones unless override=True. dotenv_values() returns the parsed values as a dict without touching the environment, and both can read from a stream such as StringIO or a network source. The .env syntax is Bash-like, supporting quoted and multiline values, comments, the export prefix, and ${VAR} variable expansion with defined precedence rules. It also offers IPython magics (%load_ext dotenv, %dotenv) and a dotenv CLI for set, list (including JSON output), and run. Setting PYTHON_DOTENV_DISABLED=1 turns off load_dotenv loading.
use_cases: load development configuration from a .env file
keep secrets out of source code
read config into a dict without changing environment
edit .env files from the command line
run a Python program with .env variables
load environment variables in IPython notebooks
parse configuration from a stream or network source
notable: Variable expansion with documented precedence depending on override setting
Can parse configuration from streams, not just files
Built-in CLI with set, list (text or JSON), and run subcommands
Supports reading from FIFOs (named pipes) on Unix
PYTHON_DOTENV_DISABLED switch for production or third-party calls
caveats: The .env file format is not formally specified and still changing over time
Reading from FIFOs is stated as supported only on Unix systems
CLI requires the separate [cli] install extra
